_note_gates_empty_: 0 of 12 candidates cleared all three gates. This is the result, not a stub. Adding any of the 12 anyway would either false-block (C02, C08, C09), never fire (C05, C12), or silently require a new engine checker - which is [[58]] case-legislation and [[05]] engine modification.

quotes: If the status is **delayed** or **on time**, the flight has not taken off, cannot be booked.
If the status is **flying**, the flight has taken off but not landed, cannot be booked.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: resolve_field calls the producer with exactly one argument; get_flight_status needs two (date, flight_number). The gated value also lives inside args['flights'] (a list of segments), not in a scalar id argument. No set-comparison over a single top-level field can express it.
_rejection_ledger_.unlock_op: multi_arg_producer + per-element iteration over a list argument

quotes: Basic economy flights cannot be modified.
In other cases, all reservations, including basic economy, can change cabin without changing the flights.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: tool-operation polysemy. One write tool performs BOTH 'change flights' (forbidden while cabin is basic economy) and 'change cabin' (explicitly permitted for basic economy by the second quote). A tool-level allow-set on the reservation's cabin therefore FALSE-BLOCKS the permitted operation. Telling the two operations apart requires diffing the `flights` argument against the stored flights = a new checker. Secondary defect: the reservation-level cabin field name is not attested by any allowed source (see _unknown_).
_rejection_ledger_.unlock_op: operation-discriminator (arg-vs-record diff) so a polysemous write tool can carry per-operation preconditions
_rejection_ledger_.near_miss_note: An `applies_when {arg:'cabin', in:['basic economy']}` + `allow:['economy','business']` encoding fits the existing declaration slots and would not false-block. It is HELD, not adopted: its condition (the call keeps cabin unchanged, therefore the caller is changing flights) is an inference, not a verbatim policy statement, so the declaration fails gate 1 even though the sentence it leans on passes.

_rejection_ledger_.state_of: flights nested inside the reservation record
quotes: Cabin cannot be changed if any flight in the reservation has already been flown.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: existential quantifier over a nested list. resolve_field returns one top-level field; membership in `allow` cannot express 'no element of reservation.flights has status flown'.
_rejection_ledger_.unlock_op: exists_where / all_where over a nested list field

quotes: The user can add but not remove checked bags.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: order comparison between an argument (total_baggages) and stored state. The engine has membership only; the `constraints` kind ops are {disjoint, equal_len} and both compare two ARGUMENTS, never an argument against a record.

quotes: The user cannot add insurance after initial booking.
_rejection_ledger_.g2_why: No tool to gate. Across the full 14-tool airline inventory, `insurance` appears as an argument of book_reservation ONLY. There is no post-booking insurance tool, so a declaration here would point at nothing and could never fire. This is the airline instance of the banking failure mode (11 of 38 A3 rows aimed at absent tools).
_rejection_ledger_.unlock_op: none - the rule is env-mirrored by the absence of the tool

quotes: The user can modify passengers but cannot modify the number of passengers.
Even a human agent cannot modify the number of passengers.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: length equality between an argument list and a stored list. `equal_len` exists but compares two arguments; there is no arg-vs-record form.

_rejection_ledger_.state_of: flights nested inside the reservation record
quotes: If any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: existential quantifier over a nested list, same shape as C03.
_rejection_ledger_.unlock_op: exists_where / all_where over a nested list field

quotes: Otherwise, flight can be cancelled if any of the following is true:
- The booking was made within the last 24 hrs
- The flight is cancelled by airline
- It is a business flight
- The user has travel insurance and the reason for cancellation is covered by insurance.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: four-way disjunction. `allow` is a NECESSARY condition (deny when cur not in allow), so encoding any single disjunct false-blocks the other three. The disjunction also mixes a time computation (created_time vs now, 24 hrs) and an OPEN predicate (whether the stated reason is covered by insurance - a judgement, LLM territory per [[52]]/[[22]]).
_rejection_ledger_.unlock_op: allow_any_of over several resolver paths - and even then one disjunct stays open

quotes: Only compensate if the user is a silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business.
Do not compensate if the user is regular member and has no travel insurance and flies (basic) economy.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: three-way disjunction spanning TWO records (user.membership, reservation.insurance, reservation.cabin) while a check names exactly one resolver_path. `allow:['silver','gold']` on [user_id, get_user_details, membership] is closed and tempting, but it is one disjunct, not the necessary condition: it would deny a regular member who holds travel insurance, whom the policy explicitly permits to be compensated.
_rejection_ledger_.unlock_op: allow_any_of across multiple resolver paths (multi-record disjunction)

quotes: Other reservations can be modified without changing the origin, destination, and trip type.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: argument-vs-record equality on three fields, and worse: update_reservation_flights takes only (cabin, flights, payment_id, reservation_id) - origin, destination and trip type are not call arguments at all, so they would first have to be DERIVED from the flights list. Derivation is not set comparison.
_rejection_ledger_.unlock_op: unchanged_fields (arg-derived vs record) - requires a derivation step first

quotes: All payment methods must already be in user profile for safety reasons.
The payment method must already be in user profile for safety reasons.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: member_of: an argument value must belong to a SET resolved from another record. The engine compares a resolved value against a literal allow-list; the direction is reversed and the right-hand side is dynamic. retail's own G7 note already records this exact op as excluded (payment member_of = derived field, [[05]] risk, not included).

quotes: Cabin class must remain the same across all the flights in the same reservation; changing cabin for just one flight segment is not possible.
_rejection_ledger_.g3_why: vacuous / env-mirrored. update_reservation_flights takes a single scalar `cabin` for the whole call, so no call can express a per-segment cabin. A gate here would never fire. A declaration that cannot fire is worse than none - it inflates A2 volume without changing a single message, which is this strand's whole premise (banking bought a 46x A2 for a 4x delivery).
_rejection_ledger_.unlock_op: none - already enforced by the tool signature

_out_of_strand_.quote: Each reservation can have at most five passengers.
_out_of_strand_.why: pure-argument cardinality; belongs to the `constraints` gate kind, not `preconditions`. Would need a max_len op.

_out_of_strand_.quote: Each reservation can use at most one travel certificate, at most one credit card, and at most three gift cards.
_out_of_strand_.why: pure-argument typed counting; needs a count_by_type op the engine does not have.

_out_of_strand_.quote: Cabin class must be the same across all the flights in a reservation.
_out_of_strand_.why: env-mirrored by the single scalar `cabin` argument (same reason as C12).

_out_of_strand_.quote: then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user.
_out_of_strand_.why: ADJACENT GAP, reported not adopted: retail declares this as G4_TRANSFER_MSG (kind=notice) and airline does not, although the airline policy carries the identical sentence and the engine's notice machinery is domain-general. This is the `notice` strand, not the state strand - handed off, not authored here.

_out_of_strand_.quote: The API does not check that cancellation rules are met, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API!
_out_of_strand_.why: the policy itself states the environment does NOT enforce the cancellation rules. That is exactly the condition under which a scaffold gate pays - and exactly the rule (C08) that gate 3 rejects. Recorded because it names what is being left on the table.

_out_of_strand_.quote: The API does not check these for the agent, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API!

_note_op_demand_: No single closed op unlocks more than 2 of the 12. Retail's four state rules all collapse to ONE op (scalar field in allow-set) because retail names one tool per lifecycle state (cancel_pending_*, modify_pending_*, return_delivered_*, exchange_delivered_*). Airline routes several operations with opposite preconditions through one write tool and keeps its state in nested lists. The axis does not fail to transfer for lack of a declaration - it is eight checkers away.
